title: Tanzanian Coconut Basted Fish
community: Zanzibar and the Swahili coast — the most iconic Tanzanian fish dish
author: Chef Fatuma

heritage.history: Samaki wa Kupaka is the fish equivalent of Kuku wa Kupaka — a whole snapper or kingfish marinated in Zanzibar spices, grilled over charcoal, and repeatedly basted with coconut-tamarind sauce until magnificently lacquered. It is the signature fish dish of Zanzibar and one of the most celebrated seafood preparations in East Africa. The Forodhani Gardens night market is famous for it.

desc: Samaki wa Kupaka — Zanzibar's most iconic fish dish. Whole fish marinated in Zanzibar spices, grilled over charcoal, and repeatedly basted with a rich coconut-tamarind sauce until deeply lacquered, smoky, and fragrant. The Swahili coast at its absolute finest.
longDesc: Samaki wa Kupaka is what happens when the Indian Ocean's finest fish meets Zanzibar's world-class spices and the ancient coastal technique of layered coconut-tamarind basting. At Zanzibar's Forodhani night market, the smell of samaki wa kupaka grilling over charcoal fills the warm night air.
ingredients: 1 large whole fish (1—1.5 kg) — snapper or kingfish, scored
steps: Score fish deeply on both sides. Rub marinade all over and into scores. Marinate 2 hours.
Make basting sauce: simmer all sauce ingredients 8 minutes. Divide in two.
Grill fish skin-side down without moving for 8—10 minutes.
Continue grilling and basting 15—20 more minutes, building layer upon layer of glaze.
chefTips: Medium coals only — coconut milk sugars burn at high heat.
Multiple thin baste layers create the lacquer.
cookingScience: Each baste layer caramelises on the fish surface through Maillard reaction. Multiple thin layers build a complex, multi-layered glaze — far more intense than a single thick application.
culturalNote: Samaki wa Kupaka is the food memory every visitor to Zanzibar carries home — the fish grilled at Forodhani since the Sultanate era. To eat it at the water's edge as dhows pass in the evening is to understand why Zanzibar is called the Spice Island.
